title: Coreceptor-assisted Lck delivery to the TCR (Artyomov et al., 2010)
reference: Artyomov MN, Lis M, Devadas S, Davis MM, Chakraborty AK (2010). CD4 and CD8 binding to MHC molecules primarily acts to enhance Lck delivery. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 107:16916-16921. doi:10.1073/pnas.1010568107

koffAg__FREE.note: TCR-pMHC dissociation for agonist peptide, /s; the parameter the paper varies to separate affinity from Lck delivery

koffCD__FREE.note: pMHC-coreceptor dissociation, /s; the x axis of the paper's Fig. 2A

konLck_local__FREE.note: coreceptor-TCR association with MHC involved, /s per chamber

konLck1_local__FREE.note: coreceptor-TCR association with no MHC involved, /s per chamber; the weakest direction here, since against koffLck of 1 /s this path holds only about two of the hundred coreceptors at equilibrium

koffLck__FREE.note: coreceptor-TCR dissociation, /s; with the association rates it sets how long Lck is held at an engaged receptor

notes: Six free parameters at almost no cost per trajectory: seventeen species, and a fit spends well under a minute, which makes this the collection's cheapest problem and a reasonable place to check that a new method works at all. The difficulty is in the structure rather than the size. The three bonds close a ring, and each has both an across-complexes rule and a ring-closing rule at a higher per-chamber rate, so an association constant acts through two different paths, and the two coreceptor-TCR on rates are separated only by which path a trajectory took. Counts are small -- ten agonist pMHC, a hundred coreceptors, a ring population peaking near one molecule -- so the observables are genuinely noisy even though every parameter is identifiable.
